newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Conrail seen going to CSX.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Conrail seen going to CSX.

text.p: Trading in Conrail Inc options suggested investors were betting that a bid for the company from the CSX Corp bid would win out over a higher bid from Norfolk Southern Corp, traders said Friday.
Early Friday, Norfolk Southern said it raised its all-cash offer for Conrail to $110 a share from $100.
On Wednesday, Conrail and CSX said they revised their October merger pact, raising the cash portion of the CSX bid.
The new CSX offer valued Conrail at around $93 a share, traders said.
Conrail shares were up 2-1/8 at 95-1/8 at 1125 CST (1725 GMT) Friday. Turnover topped 1.3 million shares.

"What's interesting is that if Norfolk's deal went through, the stock would be 110 and, depending on where you value CSX, if they win, the stock would probably be somewhere around 93," one options trader said.
He said that with the stock trading closer to 93, investors are betting a judge will dismiss Norfolk's suit to block the proposed CSX acquisition.
Conrail options trading is also indicating the same outcome, traders said.
The Conrail November 95 call was most active, with about 4,640 contracts changing hands by 1125 CST (1725 GMT).
The option, with open interest of about 10,100, was up 1/8 at 1-3/8.
"The Nov 95 calls are the most active option (and) are only trading at 1-3/8 so they're sort of implying that there will be no news until next week," the trader said.
November options expire November 15.
"The Dec 95's, at 3-5/8, will go to almost 15 if the judge rules in favor of Norfolk," he said.
"So given they're at 3-5/8, they're implying pretty low probability that they'll go with Norfolk," he said.
He added that he was short Conrail on expectations that the CSX bid would eventually win out, the same outcome the options trading is suggesting.
"If truth and justice breaks out we're going to lose a lot of money, but we think the judge is going to rule that they don't have to sell the company to the highest bidder," he said.
Conrail said Thursday its November 12 court hearing with Norfolk Southern was postponed until November 18.
Elsewhere, Iomega Corp options were busy as the company's stock listing switched to the New York Stock Exchange from the Nasdaq market.
Iomega options trade on four of the five options exchanges and the November 25 call traded a total of about 6,300 contracts. The December 25 call traded around 3,000 contracts on all exchanges.
Shares of the company were down 3/8 at 25 on heavy volume of 5.85 million shares.
